title: Understanding Blood Pressure
hook: High blood pressure is called the 'silent killer' for a reason — it usually has no symptoms, yet it quietly raises your risk of heart attack and stroke.
key_points: Blood pressure is written as two numbers: systolic (top) over diastolic (bottom).
Normal is below 120/80 mmHg; readings climb through 'elevated' into high blood pressure.
High blood pressure usually causes no symptoms, so it must be measured to be found.
It's a leading risk factor for heart attack, stroke, and kidney disease — and it's manageable.
content_html: Blood pressure is one of those numbers everyone has heard of but few can interpret. It's worth understanding, because it's one of the most important — and most silent — signals about your heart health.
extra_html: The American Heart Association explains that blood pressure is recorded as two numbers: systolic (the top number, the pressure when your heart beats) over diastolic (the bottom number, the pressure when it rests between beats), measured in millimeters of mercury. A normal reading is below 120/80; from there, readings move into "elevated," then stages of high blood pressure (hypertension). The danger is that hypertension usually produces no symptoms at all, which is why it can only be caught by actually measuring it — at a checkup, a pharmacy, or with a home monitor. Left unchecked, it's a leading driver of heart attacks, strokes, heart failure, and kidney disease. The hopeful flip side is that it's highly manageable through lifestyle changes and, when needed, medication.

related.title: Preventing Type 2 Diabetes
related.hook: Type 2 diabetes often arrives slowly, with a warning stage called prediabetes — and at that stage, modest lifestyle changes can stop or delay it.

related.title: Building a Balanced Plate
related.hook: Forget counting every calorie — the simplest healthy-eating tool is a picture of a plate: half produce, a quarter grains, a quarter protein.

related.title: Why Regular Checkups Matter
related.hook: The whole point of a checkup is to catch trouble while it's still quiet — before symptoms show up and while it's easiest to treat.

related.title: The Real Cause of a Common Stroke May Have Been Missed for Decades
related.hook: A common type of stroke may not be mainly caused by fatty plaque after all — the strongest link was found with damaged small blood vessels deep in the brain.

flashcards.prompt: What do the two numbers in a blood pressure reading mean?
flashcards.back_html: The top number is systolic (pressure when the heart beats); the bottom is diastolic (pressure between beats). Normal is below 120/80 mmHg.

flashcards.prompt: Why is high blood pressure called the 'silent killer'?

choices.text: It usually has no symptoms but raises serious health risks
It causes obvious pain that's easy to ignore

flashcards.explanation_html: High blood pressure typically produces no warning signs, so people can have it for years while it damages arteries, the heart, and kidneys — which is why it must be measured.
